# en-semiformal

## Good example

To: Warehouse and Finance leads
From: Priya Example, Stores
Subject: Stop using the old goods-received book from Monday

The paper goods-received book is going away on Monday 16 November 2026, and I need your help with the last week of it.

Here's what pushed me. In October we paid Sample Fasteners twice for the same delivery ($3,180 each time), because one receipt was written in the book at Bay 2 and the other was keyed into SampleStock at Bay 4. Finance caught it three weeks later. Nobody did anything wrong. We just had two places to record one thing.

From Monday, SampleStock is the only record. The two tablets at Bay 2 are already set up, and Luis has put a laminated login card on each. If SampleStock is down, write the delivery on the yellow pad at the Stores window and I'll key it in that afternoon.

I don't want the old book thrown out. Please bring any loose pages to me by Friday, since Finance needs them for the year-end count on 4 December.

## Pair 1

### Before

MEMO

To: Procurement Team
From: Procurement Management
Subject: Vendor Performance Review - Sample Catering Ltd

Dear team,

I hope this message finds you well. This memo provides a comprehensive overview of the vendor performance review meeting on 4 November 2026, where we conducted an assessment of how Sample Catering Ltd has performed under the current catering contract.

It is important to note that the team noted 2 late deliveries in October. They did not cause major disruption, but they are relevant to our overall assessment of the vendor's service levels and should be recorded in the formal performance file.

Moreover, the contract with Sample Catering Ltd ends on 31 December 2026. Furthermore, the review outcome will inform our decisions about the next procurement cycle, including whether to extend, retender, or adjust the service requirements.

Each team member should send their performance notes to the Procurement lead by 16 November 2026. Please include any observations on delivery timeliness, quality of service, and responsiveness to queries, along with any issues that were escalated during the contract period.

[cut]

### After

MEMO

To: Procurement Team
From: Procurement Management
Subject: Vendor Performance Review - Sample Catering Ltd

Dear team,

This memo covers the vendor performance review meeting on 4 November 2026, where we assessed how Sample Catering Ltd has performed under the current catering contract.

The team noted 2 late deliveries in October. They didn't cause major disruption, but they're relevant to our overall assessment of the vendor's service levels and should be recorded in the formal performance file.

The contract with Sample Catering Ltd ends on 31 December 2026. The review outcome will inform our decisions about the next procurement cycle, including whether to extend, retender, or adjust the service requirements.

Each team member should send their performance notes to the Procurement lead by 16 November 2026. Please include any observations on delivery timeliness, quality of service, and responsiveness to queries, along with any issues that were escalated during the contract period.

We'll share the consolidated notes with the team once we've received them. If you have any questions about the review or the required format, please contact the Procurement lead directly.

## Pair 2

### Before

Weekly Procurement Meeting - Progress Briefing

Good morning, everyone. In today's fast-paced procurement landscape, this briefing provides an update on where our 2026 procurement packages stand ahead of this week's meeting.

Overall status

Of the 12 packages planned for 2026, 8 are now under contract. That is two thirds of the programme successfully completed, which is a truly solid position as we approach the final weeks of the year.

Moreover, three packages are currently out to tender. Furthermore, they are moving through the evaluation and selection stages, and we expect to report on their outcomes as the process moves forward.

One package is on hold because funding is not available yet. The team will keep monitoring the budget position before going ahead with it.

Target

Our target is for all packages to be under contract by 15 December 2026. Based on the current position, this is still achievable, although it depends on the timely completion of the three tenders in progress and on the resolution of the funding position for the package on hold.

Next steps

### After

Weekly Procurement Meeting - Progress Briefing

Good morning, everyone. Here's where our 2026 procurement packages stand ahead of this week's meeting.

Overall status

Of the 12 packages planned for 2026, 8 are now under contract. That's two thirds of the programme successfully completed, which is a solid position as we approach the final weeks of the year.

Three packages are currently out to tender. They're moving through the evaluation and selection stages, and we expect to report on their outcomes as the process moves forward.

One package is on hold because funding isn't available yet. The team will keep monitoring the budget position before going ahead with it.

Target

Our target is for all packages to be under contract by 15 December 2026. Based on the current position, this is still achievable, although it depends on the three tenders in progress finishing on time and on the funding position for the package on hold being resolved.

Next steps
